segments.he:
א.

כְּשֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים נִתְפַּרְסְמִים בָּעוֹלָם, עַל-יְדֵי- זֶה נִתְחַדְּשִׁים נִגּוּנִים בָּעוֹלָם. ב.

הַלְוִיִּים הָיָה לָהֶם לְכָל יוֹם נִגּוּן מְיֻחָד, וְעַכְּשֶׁו בַּגָלוּת נִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ הַנִּגּוּנִים. וּכְּשֶׁבָּאָה אֵיזֶהוּ שֶׁבֶר עַל אֵיזֶהוּ אֻמָּה, אֲזַי מִתְנוֹצֵץ הַנִּגּוּן שֶׁל הַלְוִיִּים שֶּׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד הַשֶּׁבֶר הַזֶּה.
segments.en:
When Tzaddikim are publicized in the world, through this new melodies are brought into the world.

segments.he:
ג.

עַל-יְדֵי הַנִּגּוּנִים שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם קוֹל בְּכִיָּה, יְכוֹלִים לְהוֹצִיא הַשְּׁבוּיִים, בְּחִינַת מוֹצִיא אֲסִירִים בַּכּוֹשָׁרוֹת.
segments.en: The Leviim had a special melody designated for each day, but now, in the Exile, the melodies have been forgotten. When some tragedy comes upon some nation, the melody of the Leviim corresponding to that crisis is aroused (lit. sparks or glistens).

segments.he:
ד.

עַל-יְדֵי הַנְּגִינָה אָדָם נִכָּר, אִם קִבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל תּוֹרָה.
segments.en: Through the melodies that contain a tone of crying, it is possible to release the captives, the aspect of "He brings out prisoners bakosharot (in a kosher – propitious – time).” [t.n. The word bakosharot  is split into two words (by the Medrash): bekhi – meaning crying, shirot – meaning song = song with a crying tone].

segments.he:
ה.

מַה כְּשֶׁאָדָם שׁוֹתֶה, מַתְחִיל לְזַמֵּר וּלְנַגֵּן וְלֹא כֵן בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁירָה עַל הַבְּאֵר, וְלֹא אָמְרוּ שִׁירָה עַל הַמָּן.
segments.en:
Through song, a person can be discerned if he accepted upon himself the yoke of Torah.

That which a person when he drinks begins to sing and make melody (music), which is not so when he eats -- this is because they (the Jews in the desert) expressed shira (song of praise and gratitude to G-d) over the Well, and not over the Manna.
